ai_overview.text:
The average recruiter in the United States makes between $60,000 and $110,000 per year in total compensation. However, how much a recruiter makes depends entirely on the type of recruiting they do, their industry, and how their commission is structured. Payscale +4 The career path splits into two primary models: steady, predictable corporate salaries, and volatile, high-ceiling agency commissions. Try Kondo Corporate (In-House) Recruiters : These recruiters work directly for one company (like Google or Amazon) to fill internal roles. They enjoy a steady income consisting of a base salary and an annual performance bonus.Average Total Pay: $100,000 – $162,000/year. Glassdoor +4 Average Total Pay: $100,000 – $162,000/year. Glassdoor +4 Agency (Third-Party) Recruiters : These recruiters work for staffing firms (like Aerotek or Insight Global) to find talent for multiple client companies. They operate heavily on a commission-based pay structure.Average Total Pay: $50,000 – $90,000/year for standard billers; $150,000 – $250,000+/year for top performers. Reddit · r/recruiting +4 Average Total Pay: $50,000 – $90,000/year for standard billers; $150,000 – $250,000+/year for top performers. Reddit · r/recruiting +4 Executive Search Recruiters : These specialized recruiters target high-level, C-suite executives. Because executive salaries are massive, these recruiters command the highest commissions in the industry.Average Total Pay: $110,000 – $300,000+/year. Quora +2 Average Total Pay: $110,000 – $300,000+/year. Quora +2 The compensation mechanics differ drastically based on the employer's model: nTech Workforce Compensation Model Typical Structure Earnings Potential Pros & Cons
Salary + Bonus (Corporate)90% base salary + 10% annual cash bonus. Stable, but capped. Top earnings scale slowly with promotions. High stability, great benefits, but no massive windfalls.
Base + Commission (Agency)Low base (~$45k–$55k) + percentage of fees billed. Highly variable. Average performers double their base; top performers make six figures. High pressure. If you do not hit quotas or "draws," you can be let go.
Pure Commission (Independent)0% base salary. Recruiters keep 30% to 70% of the placement fee. Unlimited. Can range from $0 to $500,000+ per year. Extreme risk. No steady paycheck, requiring a massive network to survive. When an agency recruiter places a permanent employee at a company, the agency charges a fee—typically 15% to 25% of that candidate's first-year salary. Juicebox +1 Recruiters who specialize in complex, high-paying industries earn significantly more than generalists.
